sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (primary; no consensus):** TSMC FY2025 Form 20-F via SEC EDGAR XBRL (CIK 1046179) FY22-24 statements; TSMC IR quarterly pages for FY2025, H1-2026 actuals, FY2026 guidance. WebSearch returned empty bodies; one earnings PDF 404'd; anything not pulled from a primary source is [UNAVAILABLE], never guessed.

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS (first):** Accruals (NI−CFO)/avg assets = −7.4% (FY23), −10.9% (FY24); CFO/NI 1.46x→1.58x — deep, worsening (cash outruns NI via large D&A add-back), a quality POSITIVE. No divergence; margin up WITH better cash conversion. Taiwan-domiciled consolidated 20-F filer, not PRC/HFCAA; KPMG long-tenured; no material-weakness flag. No related-party extraction. **Gate clears.**

**Revenue (>70% of value — foundry demand):** FY2025 Q1 $25.53, Q2 $30.07, Q3 $33.10, Q4 $33.73bn = **$122.43bn (+38.7% vs FY24 $88.27bn)**. FY2026 Q1 $35.90, Q2 $40.20bn, Q3 guide $44.6-45.8bn; +~$48-50bn Q4 ⇒ **FY2026E ≈ $170bn ≈ +39% YoY** on a verified H1 base. AI/HPC-led; not extrapolated as forever-rate.

**Margins:** GM FY24 56.1% → FY25 ~59.5% → FY26 Q1 66.2% / Q2 67.7% (guide 65-67%). OM FY24 45.7% → FY25 ~50.7% → FY26 Q1 58.1% / Q2 60.3%. **FY2026E OM ~58% (op ≈ $99.5bn).** Question: is 66-68% GM / 58-60% OM a NEW structural plateau or a cyclic peak? DCF runs both; base fades OM to ~50-51%; I do not assume the 60% peak is permanent.

**Tax/capex:** Effective tax ~12.4% (model ~13%, Arizona drag). D&A FY24 $19.9bn rising. Capex FY24 $29.2bn = **33% of revenue** (load-bearing capital anchor); FCF $55.7bn CFO − $29.2bn = $26.5bn (thin over a semi-fixed, fast capex base — the fragility the kill targets).

**EPS/ADS:** FY24 US$6.90; FY25E ~$10.2; **FY2026E ≈ $86bn × 0.865 ÷ 5.19bn ADS ≈ $16.6/ADS.** At $430 entry ≈ **25.9x FY2026E, ~42x trailing FY25E** — the multiple already prices a bullish structural-AI view.

**Valuation (FCFF DCF, COE 9%, terminal g 3.5%, 6y):** Base (OM fade 58→50%): EV ≈$2.0-2.1tr + $120bn net cash ⇒ **~$418-445/ADS = current price, no margin of safety.** Structural (OM ~54%): EV ≈$2.44tr ⇒ **~$494/ADS (+15% over entry).** Sensitivity: rev −15% FY27 → sub-$400; COE 9%±50bp ≈ ±8%. Decisive: is the margin hold structural.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.markdown: Market believes TSMC is the dominant advanced-node foundry in a structural AI supercycle — near-monopoly 3nm/5nm pricing power, every US hyperscaler fabbed here, already +66%/12m, Taiwan/China risks distant tails — a crowded mega-cap only the cycle itself can hurt.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** 66-68% GM / 58-60% OM and +30-40% revenue are the durable AI-supercycle new normal; ~26x forward reasonable; the run continues; China/geopolitical risk near-zero.

**Why wrong:** We agree direction and margins are real (Q2'26 $40.2bn, GM 67.7%, OM 60.3% — filing-confirmed); we differ on PRICE and CYCLE READ. (a) GM 67.7% is ~12-14pp above FY24's 56.1%; even partial reversion to FY25 (~59.5/50.7) cuts FY27E EPS ~25%, and it's priced for a PERMANENT plateau. (b) Our base-case DCF (~$418-445) ≈ current price ($433.24) — **no margin of safety**; the only upside leg underwrites the more aggressive structural-AI hold as base: thin, momentum-flavoured at cyclic-peak margins. Screen tags `china_growth` under no-reflation China (macro_regime 2026-09-12) but marginal demand is US/HPC-led — the tag is the wrong box, not cheapness; if systematics discount TSM as China-beta, a modest structural-flow component exists.

**Proves us wrong:** if FY2026 H2 margins HOLD 65-68% GM / 56-60% OM through Q3 (2026-10-15) and Q4 with strong AI commentary, AND ~26x forward holds/extends without reverting toward our ~20x anchor — the market underwrites the structural plateau and we are wrong to stop at +15%. The margin-hold is the crux.

sections.heading: Edge taxonomy
sections.markdown: **(a) Analytical** — the discipline is the CYCLE READ and price paid: we run margin-fade vs margin-hold DCF and show the base case is fully priced (no MoS), not just endorsing momentum. Secondary (d) structural-flow: the `china_growth` mislabel on a US-AI name. NOT (b) strong informational-synthesis, NOT (c) time-arbitrage rescuing valuation. **Honest:** momentum-continuation at cyclic-peak margins, base case fully priced; momentum is the book's weakest edge (procyclical). Our numbers land this LOW/zero expected-value long — reported as a finding, not hidden.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.markdown:
1. Margin fragility: Q2'26 GM 67.7% / OM 60.3% (IR) vs FY24 GM 56.1% / OM 45.7% (20-F) — even partial reversion to FY25 (~59.5/50.7) cuts forward EPS ~25% AND compresses ~26x simultaneously; −30% at kill is a floor, not a ceiling.
2. Capital intensity + thin FCF: FY24 capex $29.2bn = 33% of revenue, D&A $19.9bn, CFO $55.7bn → FCF $26.5bn (20-F). Capex semi-fixed; a demand ramp-down doesn't retire the committed buildout, so FCF collapses faster than revenue in a rollover.
3. Base case fully priced: $433.24 spot vs ~$418-445 base-case DCF — no margin of safety; only the structural-AI leg (+15% to $494) is upside, requiring a plateau ~12-14pp above FY24.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is mid-2027 and this long lost ~30% — kill (~$300) fired. Most likely we were RIGHT AI demand was real but WRONG the 2026 margin plateau (~67% GM / ~60% OM) was structural — as leading-edge capacity came on and hyperscaler ordering normalized, GM reverted toward ~56-60% and OM ~50%, hitting BOTH legs (EPS −25% AND the multiple compressed toward ~20x), so a ~30% drawdown arrived faster than the +15% structural case could bank. Secondary: the `china_growth`-tagged exposure plus a Taiwan escalation widened the discount as the crowded AI trade unwound (momentum-crash risk), and thin FCF over fixed 33% capex gave no buffer. The margin-hold was the load-bearing bet; I flag it first for Drew.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_MOMENTUM_CONTINUATION attack on T-GLOBAL-TSM-001**

1. **The long is negative-EV by the thesis's own arithmetic.** ev_math: p_up 0.50/up 15% vs p_down 0.50/down −30% ⇒ expected −7.3%; own-Kelly −171bp; quarter-Kelly = 0. A model that says a position loses ~7% on expectation cannot support a long entry. Defending the long requires proving the down-probability legs are wrong — the thesis never does; it asserts them with the cash-69-margin asymmetry (up 15 / down 30).

2. **The valuation is circular with the screen.** The same H1-26 margins feed the +66% momentum screen AND the DCF. Base case (~$418–445) ≈ spot ($433). Every outcome converges on "fully priced"; only the structural leg (+15% to $494) is upside, and it REQUIRES OM to hold ~12–14pp above FY24 baseline. Falsifiable challenge: cite any foundry cycle since 2000 where OM stayed that far above its mid-cycle baseline for two+ years — TSMC's own history (FY23 OM ~41%, FY24 ~45.7%) says no.

3. **Kill at $300 is not a −30% floor; realistic rollover is worse.** Reversion to FY25 (~59.5 GM/50.7 OM) cuts FY27E EPS ~25% AND compresses ~26x toward ~20x simultaneously — that is ~40–45% combined, not 30%. The $300 kill sits atop the down-probability mass, not below it. The thesis understates its own downside; −30% is the mean, not the tail.

4. **No dated catalyst justifies paying full value today.** The sole review trigger is Q3 earnings (2026-10-15); nothing between now and then is a priced, incremental, falsifiable event. Entry at $430, max-chase 3%, no MoS, peak margins — this is momentum chase at the exact moment the thesis admits the multiple already prices the bullish case. Falsifiable: name the catalyst in the next 4 weeks that is not already in the price.

5. **The edge taxonomy is self-refuting.** It concedes momentum is "the book's weakest edge (procyclical)," tags `china_growth` (systematics = China-beta discount), and its edge is "analytical discipline" on a fully-priced name. Discipline that yields quarter-Kelly = 0 recommends no-position, not long. Absent a specific, dated, falsifiable mispricing, a live long fails below the bar the thesis itself sets.

**Verdict: KILL_RECOMMENDED**
The thesis's own numbers (negative expected value, zero Kelly, base case = spot, margin-hold as the only upside) describe a fully-priced, no-catalyst long whose realistic downside exceeds its stated −30% kill; there is no honest edge to justify opening the position.
